project.objective: Did Santiago Gonzalez and his wife Petra Tumbaco of Guayaquil, Ecuador have a son named Manuel de Jesus, born 1915, in addition to their two known daughters (b. 1921 and 1934)?

questions.question: Did Santiago Gonzalez and Petra Tumbaco of Guayaquil, Ecuador have a son named Manuel de Jesus born approximately 1915?
questions.rationale: The research objective asks whether this couple had a son named Manuel de Jesus (b. ~1915) beyond their two known daughters (Maria Angela b. ~1921 and Maria Bartola b. ~1934). No sources exist yet for this family. Ecuador civil registration began in 1901, so birth records for 1915 Guayaquil should exist in the civil registry held by FamilySearch. Church baptismal registers (Catholic parishes of Guayaquil) and census-type records may also confirm or deny the birth. This is the primary and only question needed to answer the research objective.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: Two independent original civil death certificates from the Registro Civil de Guayaquil (src_001: acta 6059/1985 for Manuel de Jesus; src_002: acta 1917/2003 for Bartola) confirm Santiago Gonzalez and Petra/Petita Tumbaco as parents of children bearing the compound surname Gonzalez Tumbaco. The two certificates were issued 18 years apart by different registrants for different deaths — independent informant pathways. Church baptism collection (1520610) and Catholic Church Records (1923402) searched online with nil results, consistent with loc_001 finding that Guayaquil city baptism registers are not digitized on FamilySearch. Census collection (5000097) contains only 19th-century data. Marriage records (1520614) searched. FAN search (daughters' baptisms) attempted. Full-text search skipped: loc_001 confirms Guayaquil baptism registers are not in the FamilySearch corpus. Physical Registro Civil de Guayas (pli_008) skipped: not accessible via automated tools; civil birth certificate for 1915 birth would require in-person visit. Original images examined and confirmed (log_008, log_009).

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: YES. Two original civil death certificates from the Registro Civil de Guayaquil independently confirm Manuel de Jesus Gonzalez Tumbaco (b. 1915, d. 5 Dec 1985) as a son of Santiago Gonzalez and Petra/Petita Tumbaco. The compound surname Gonzalez Tumbaco (paternal+maternal) encodes the parentage directly. Age at death (70 in 1985) corroborates birth year 1915.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: YES. FamilySearch collections searched: Ecuador Catholic Church Records (1923402), Ecuador Baptisms 1680-1930 (1520610), Ecuador Cemetery Records 1862-2020 (3755446), Ecuador Census 1737-1990 (5000097), Ecuador Marriages 1680-1930 (1520614). Original images read for both positive records. Full-text search skipped (Guayaquil baptisms not in FamilySearch corpus per loc_001). Physical Registro Civil marked inaccessible. Breadth is constrained by digitization gaps documented in loc_001, not by research choices.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: YES. Both initial source entries were derivative (FamilySearch indexes). Original civil burial certificates were examined via FamilySearch images (log_008: ark:/61903/3:1:3QHV-D3C4-M7WX; log_009: ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C3HF-SZWT). Source classifications updated to original. Original images confirmed all indexed values; no transcription errors found for key fields (name, death date, parent names). Mother's name 'Petita Tumbaco' confirmed as written in original.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: YES. Two independent sources: (1) Civil death certificate for Manuel de Jesus (acta 6059, 5 Dec 1985), informant unknown family member at time of death registration; (2) Civil death certificate for Bartola Gonzalez Tumbaco (acta 1917, 15 Mar 2003), informant unknown family member 18 years later. Different deceased persons, different registration events, different dates, different registrants — genuinely independent informant pathways, not same-informant related items.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: YES. Both sources are original (civil death certificates issued by Registro Civil de Guayaquil). Information quality is indeterminate (informant unknown) for parent names. Evidence type for parentage assertions is direct (parent names explicitly stated, not inferred from household position). One original record with direct evidence for parentage confirmed.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: YES. The only potential conflict was 'Petita Tumbaco' (Manuel's record) vs 'Petra Tumbaco' (Bartola's record). The Bartola record independently uses the full form 'Petra,' confirming that 'Petita' is a diminutive variant of the same name. Both records name the same father (Santiago Gonzalez). No unresolved conflicts remain.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: LOW. The conclusion — that Manuel de Jesus Gonzalez Tumbaco (b. 1915) is a son of Santiago Gonzalez and Petra Tumbaco of Guayaquil — is supported by two independent original government records. No accessible unsearched record type would plausibly name different parents. The main unaccessed source (civil birth certificate from Registro Civil, pli_008) could only corroborate, not contradict; access requires in-person visit to Guayaquil.

items.rationale: Ecuador, Catholic Church Records, 1565-2023 (collection 1923402) is the largest indexed+images collection on FamilySearch and the primary online path for a Catholic baptism in Guayaquil ca. 1915. Search for Manuel de Jesus González Tumbaco (born ~1915), children of Santiago Gonzalez and Petra Tumbaco. Locality guide (loc_001) notes Guayaquil city church records have limited online coverage but this collection is the best available; a hit here is direct evidence of birth and parentage.

Ecuador, Baptisms, 1680-1930 (collection 1520610) is a separate index-only collection that may capture records not indexed in collection 1923402. Fallback for the Catholic Church Records search. Note: index only — no images attached; if a match is found, the original register must be located via FamilySearch Catalog or diocese.

Locality survey (loc_001) explicitly states that Guayaquil city church/civil birth records are NOT digitized on FamilySearch. The full-text co-occurrence search via search-full-text skill operates on FamilySearch's AI-transcribed corpus. Since Guayaquil baptism registers are not in that corpus, the search would not find Manuel de Jesus's baptism record. The question (q_001) has already been answered by two independent original civil death certificates from the Registro Civil de Guayaquil confirming parentage. Overturn risk from skipping this search is negligible: a baptism record, if found, would corroborate but not contradict the answer.

Search the Guayaquil death-record indexes for a Manuel de Jesus González Tumbaco ca. 1915-1935. Locality guide (loc_001) confirms 69 death-index volumes for Guayaquil 1901-1940 on FamilySearch, many 95-100% name-indexed. If the child died in infancy or childhood, his death record would directly confirm his birth and parentage. Absence in death records through ~1935 is also informative (suggests survival). Also search Ecuador Deaths 1800-1920 (collection 1520615). Search also covers Ecuador, Cemetery Records (3755446, indexed+images) — child burial entries typically name parents.

Ecuador, Census, 1737-1990 (collection 5000097, indexed+images) may contain a household enumeration placing Santiago Gonzalez, Petra Tumbaco, and their children together ca. 1920s-1930s. A census record naming a son Manuel de Jesus in the household would be strong corroborating evidence. Searches under 'Gonzalez' and 'Santiago Gonzalez' for Guayaquil/Guayas.

Search Ecuador, Catholic Church Records (1923402) and Ecuador Marriages (1520614) for the marriage of Santiago Gonzalez to Petra Tumbaco. Per BCG Standard 11 and the record-type guide, the parents' marriage record validates the couple as a documented unit, supplies Petra's maiden name (Tumbaco) in a primary source, and by its date relative to 1915 corroborates the feasibility of a son born that year. The couple is in the tree without source documentation; the marriage record is the foundational verification.

FAN item: Search Ecuador Catholic Church Records (1923402) for baptisms of the two known daughters — Maria Angela González Tumbaco (b. ~1921) and Maria Bartola González Tumbaco (b. ~1934). Their baptism records, if found, (a) confirm Santiago Gonzalez and Petra Tumbaco as parents in a primary source, (b) may mention siblings or family context, and (c) establish the documentary family unit against which the presence or absence of a son Manuel de Jesus can be measured. A baptism register page with multiple González Tumbaco entries is especially informative.

Physical-only repository (Registro Civil de Guayas, Guayaquil). Not accessible via any automated MCP tool. A researcher visiting Guayaquil in person could request the civil birth registration for Manuel de Jesus Gonzalez Tumbaco ca. 1915 from the Registro Civil. Skipped in the automated workflow because the question is answered by accessible online sources; this would be a recommended follow-up for independent original-record confirmation.

Father: SANTIAGO GONZALEZ. Mother: PETITA TUMBACO — confirmed as written in the original document (not a transcription error). Source is an original government document, not a derivative cemetery index. Source classification should be updated to original.

Original civil burial certificate (Certificado Simple Gratuita para la Inhumación y Sepultura) from Registro Civil de Guayaquil, Provincia de Guayas. Acta 1917, tomo 6, página 127, year 2003. Confirms: BARTOLA GONZALES TUMBACO (surname GONZALES in original, not GONZALEZ), cedula 0905532404, age 69 (birth ~1933/1934), SOLTERA, died 15 March 2003, cause: Derame Cerebral (stroke), physician Dr. Joel Suarez. Father: SANTIAGO GONZALES. Mother: PETRA TUMBACO — uses full form 'Petra' (vs. diminutive 'Petita' in Manuel's record). This is an original government document. hypotheses.claim: The name 'Petita Tumbaco' in Manuel de Jesus Gonzalez Tumbaco's 1985 civil death certificate (src_001, a_008) refers to the same person as 'Petra Tumbaco' in Bartola Gonzalez Tumbaco's 2003 civil death certificate (src_002, a_014) and tree person G6MT-HDQ.
hypotheses.notes: Evidence: (1) 'Petita' is a well-documented Spanish diminutive of 'Petra'. (2) Bartola's independent certificate (18 years later, different registrant) names the same mother as 'Petra Tumbaco' with identical surname Tumbaco. (3) Both certificates name the same father 'Santiago Gonzalez', anchoring both maternal name forms to the same family unit. (4) Original image of Manuel's certificate examined (log_008) and confirms the document reads 'PETITA TUMBACO' — not a transcription error. The convergence of diminutive recognition, shared unusual compound surname, same father across genuinely independent records, and direct image confirmation establishes that 'Petita Tumbaco' and 'Petra Tumbaco' refer to the same person.

proof_summaries.exhaustive_search_summary: Searched FamilySearch collections for Ecuador covering church baptisms (Catholic Church Records 1923402; Ecuador Baptisms 1680-1930, collection 1520610), civil/cemetery records (Ecuador Cemetery Records 1862-2020, collection 3755446), census (Ecuador Census 1737-1990, collection 5000097), and marriage (Ecuador Marriages 1680-1930, collection 1520614). FAN search attempted for known daughters' baptism records. Original civil death certificate images examined for both positive results (log_008: Manuel's certificate; log_009: Bartola's certificate). Full-text search of unindexed parish registers skipped: locality survey (loc_001) confirms Guayaquil city baptism registers are not in the FamilySearch corpus. Physical Registro Civil de Guayas (civil birth certificate for 1915 birth) not consulted — inaccessible in the automated workflow; an in-person visit to Guayaquil would be required. That civil birth certificate, if obtained, would be expected to corroborate and could advance this conclusion to the proved tier.

## Proof Summary: Did Santiago Gonzalez and Petra Tumbaco Have a Son Named Manuel de Jesus Born Approximately 1915?

### Conclusion

The preponderance of evidence strongly suggests that **Manuel de Jesus Gonzalez Tumbaco** (born approximately 1915 in Guayaquil, Ecuador; died 5 December 1985) was the son of **Santiago Gonzalez** and **Petra Tumbaco** of Guayaquil, Provincia de Guayas, Ecuador. This conclusion rests on two independent original civil death certificates issued by the Registro Civil de Guayaquil, each naming the same parents.

---

### Primary Evidence

**1. Civil Death Certificate for Manuel de Jesus Gonzalez Tumbaco (1985)**

The Registro Civil de Guayaquil recorded the death of Manuel de Jesus Gonzalez Tumbaco on 5 December 1985. The original certificate states his age as 70 years — implying a birth year of approximately 1915 (1985 − 70 = 1915), consistent with the research question — and gives his occupation as *Sastre* (tailor) and marital status as *Soltero* (single/unmarried). The cause of death was Edema Agudo del Pulmón, certified by Dr. Diogenes Layana.

The certificate explicitly states: *"Padre SANTIAGO GONZALEZ Madre PETITA TUMBACO."* The source is an original civil government record (a *Certificación Simple Gratuita para la Inhumación y Sepultura* issued by the Registro Civil). The information quality for the parent names is classified as indeterminate — the identity of the person who supplied the names to the registrant is unknown, though presumably a family member registering the death. The evidence type is direct: the parent names are explicitly stated, not inferred from household position or indirect cues.

The compound surname *Gonzalez Tumbaco* reinforces the parentage claim through the standard Spanish naming convention: the first compound surname is the paternal surname (*Gonzalez*, from Santiago Gonzalez) and the second is the maternal surname (*Tumbaco*, from Petra Tumbaco). The compound surname encodes the parentage independently of the stated parent-name fields.

*Registro Civil de Guayaquil, Provincia de Guayas, Registro de Defunciones 1985, tomo 18, página 157, acta no. 6059, entry for Manuel de Jesus Gonzalez Tumbaco; digital image, "Ecuador, Cemetery Records, 1862-2020," FamilySearch (ark:/61903/3:1:3QHV-D3C4-M7WX : accessed 3 August 2026).*

**2. Civil Death Certificate for Bartola Gonzales Tumbaco (2003)**

An independent corroborating record was identified through a broader search of Ecuador civil records. The Registro Civil de Guayaquil recorded the death of Bartola Gonzales Tumbaco on 15 March 2003. The original certificate lists her cédula as 0905532404, her approximate age as 69 years (implying birth approximately 1934), and her marital status as *Soltera*. The cause of death was Derame Cerebral (cerebral hemorrhage/stroke), certified by Dr. Joel Suarez. The note on the surname spelling: the original document consistently uses *Gonzales* (with an *s*), a common orthographic variant of *Gonzalez* in Ecuadorian civil registration.

The certificate explicitly states: *"Padre SANTIAGO GONZALES Madre PETRA TUMBACO"* — the same parents named in Manuel's certificate, this time with the full form *Petra* rather than the diminutive *Petita*.

Bartola Gonzales Tumbaco (born approximately 1934) corresponds to the known tree person Maria Bartola González Tumbaco, a previously identified daughter of Santiago Gonzalez and Petra Tumbaco. Her death registration, made eighteen years after Manuel's by a different registrant for a different death event, provides a genuinely independent informant pathway to the same parental pair. Both certificates bear the compound surname Gonzalez/Gonzales Tumbaco, encoding the same paternal and maternal lineage.

*Registro Civil de Guayaquil, Provincia de Guayas, Registro de Defunciones 2003, tomo 6, página 127, acta no. 1917, entry for Bartola Gonzales Tumbaco; digital image, "Ecuador, Cemetery Records, 1862-2020," FamilySearch (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C3HF-SZWT : accessed 3 August 2026).*

---

### Name Variant Analysis: "Petita" versus "Petra"

Manuel's certificate names his mother as *PETITA TUMBACO*; Bartola's certificate, issued eighteen years later by a different registrant, names the same mother as *PETRA TUMBACO*. *Petita* is a well-documented Spanish diminutive of *Petra*, commonly used in informal speech and sometimes captured in civil registration in Ecuador. The surname *Tumbaco* is identical in both records. The shared father *Santiago Gonzalez* (or *Gonzales*) appears in both records without variant. No evidence suggests these two name forms refer to different women. The Bartola record — by using the formal *Petra* — resolves any ambiguity about the informal *Petita* in Manuel's record: both registrations describe the same mother. The original image of Manuel's certificate (log_008) was examined and confirms the document reads 'PETITA TUMBACO', ruling out a transcription error as the source of the variant. This identification is formalized as hypothesis h_001.

---

### Negative Evidence and Search Scope

Multiple record types were searched to confirm or refute the conclusion:

- **Ecuador Baptisms 1680–1930** (FamilySearch collection 1520610): zero results for Manuel Gonzalez with parents Gonzalez/Tumbaco. This is consistent with the locality survey finding that Guayaquil city church baptism registers are not digitized on FamilySearch for this period. The absence is expected and does not contradict the positive evidence.
- **Ecuador Catholic Church Records** (collection 1923402): 142 results; none matched Manuel de Jesus Gonzalez Tumbaco with appropriate parentage. Returned records were from other provinces.
- **Ecuador Census** (collection 5000097): 38 results, all 19th-century entries. No 20th-century household enumeration for Guayaquil is available in this collection.
- **Ecuador Marriages 1680–1930** (collection 1520614): no marriage record found for Santiago Gonzalez × Petra Tumbaco. Guayaquil city marriage registers have limited online coverage per the locality survey.
- **FAN search** (baptisms for known daughter Maria Angela Gonzalez Tumbaco): negative. No baptism record found, consistent with the same digitization gaps.
- **Age anomaly on Bartola's certificate (a_021)**: The age field on Bartola's original civil death certificate appears to read *QUINCE* (15) in the image, which is arithmetically inconsistent with a birth year of approximately 1934 and death in 2003 (expected age approximately 69 years). This is likely a form-layout misread or partially filled field in the scan. It does not affect the parentage finding — the Padre and Madre fields on the same certificate are clearly legible and independently verified against Manuel's record. The researcher's arithmetic estimate of approximately 69 years is recorded as the working value pending any future re-examination of the document.

A full-text search of unindexed FamilySearch parish registers was not executed because the locality survey (loc_001) explicitly confirms that Guayaquil city baptism registers are not in the FamilySearch image corpus. A civil birth certificate for Manuel de Jesus (born approximately 1915) would be held by the Registro Civil de Guayas in Guayaquil; this physical record was not consulted in the automated research workflow. Obtaining it would require an in-person visit or mail request to the Registro Civil de Guayas. Such a record would be expected to corroborate the present finding and, if confirmed, would advance this conclusion to the proved tier.

---

### Tier: Probable

This conclusion is classified as **probable** rather than proved. Both supporting sources are original civil death certificates — an appropriate and respected record type — and both provide direct evidence of the parent names. However, the information quality for the parent names is classified as indeterminate in both records: the identity and relationship of the person who supplied the parent names to the registrant at the time of each death registration is unknown. Under GPS standards, the proved tier requires at least two independent original sources carrying primary information — that is, information supplied by a person with firsthand knowledge of the event being recorded. For the parentage claim, primary information would come from a civil birth certificate dated at or near 1915, where the registering party (typically a parent) would have firsthand knowledge of the child's parentage. That record has not been located in any accessible online repository.

The evidence nevertheless strongly points in one direction. Two independent original government records, issued eighteen years apart by different registrants for different deaths, agree on both parent names. The standard compound-surname encoding (*Gonzalez Tumbaco*) independently reflects the same parentage. No conflicting evidence was found naming different or additional parents. The conclusion represents the most defensible answer the current evidence supports.

Previously unknown evidence — particularly a civil birth certificate from the Registro Civil de Guayas, Guayaquil — may arise at any time and could alter this conclusion. Obtaining that certificate is the logical next step for a researcher visiting Guayaquil in person.

# Locality Guide: Guayaquil, Guayas, Ecuador (1900–1940)

## Key finding for q_001
Civil birth registers for Guayaquil from 1900 onward are NOT digitized on FamilySearch. The 69 FamilySearch volumes for Guayaquil in this period are ALL death/burial indexes. A birth ca. 1915 must be sought through: (1) Catholic Church Records collection 1923402 (baptism, indexed+images), (2) civil birth registers via the Registro Civil de Guayas directly, (3) death indexes if the child died young.

## Civil Registration
- Began 1900 nationally. Birth records at Registro Civil de Guayas, Guayaquil.
- NOT available online for births. Deaths: 69 volumes on FamilySearch (1901–1940), many 95–100% name-indexed.

## Church Records
- Ecuador, Catholic Church Records, 1565–2023 (FS 1923402): indexed + images — best online path for baptisms.
- Ecuador, Baptisms, 1680–1930 (FS 1520610): index only.
- Coverage for Guayaquil city specifically is limited; wiki warns city church records typically not online.

## Cemetery Records
- Ecuador, Cemetery Records, 1862–2020 (FS 3755446): indexed + images. Multiple Guayaquil cemeteries covered.

## Census
- Ecuador, Census, 1737–1990 (FS 5000097): indexed + images.

## Research Tips
- Search 'González Tumbaco' and 'Gonzalez Tumbaco' (accent variants).
- For a ca. 1915 birth not found online: contact Registro Civil de Guayas (+593 43-802-300 ext. 3200) or Dirección General del Registro Civil, Quito.
- Check death indexes for infant/child death entries naming parents — confirms or denies child's existence even if no birth record is found online.
